items.heading: ## Scheduled Work
items.text: - Operation name format for `Dispatcher.callOperation`: `<package>.<Class>#<operation>` (the `#` separates the generated class from the operation), for example `<package>.<Class>#<operation>` for a STATIC operation on an unmapped transfer object. The generated `<app>-asm.model` in `application/model/target/generated-resources/model/` lists the names.
items.evidence: judo-ng target/judo-ng-read/wt/runtime__judo-services/judo-services-simple-function-dispatcher/src/test/java/hu/blackbelt/judo/services/simple/function/dispatcher/NameingConventioBasedDispatcherImplTest.java:95 (callOperation("package1.Class1#operation1", ...)); app: webshop-test application/model/target/generated-resources/model/webshop-asm.model. Note: the catalog bullet shows callOperation(name, exchange); the app passes a HashMap of inputs, not checked in judo-ng.

items.heading: #### Pattern 4: Partial Updates
items.text: To send a partial update that keeps the version check, put the identifier and the version into the payload with the generated builder: `<Entity>Builder.from(Map.of("__identifier", <identifier>, "__entityType", "<Entity>", "__version", <version>, "<attribute>", <value>)).build()`. A `__version` in the payload makes the optimistic-lock check apply to the update; the mask only shapes the returned entity.
items.evidence: judo-ng target/judo-ng-read/wt/template__judo-psm-generator-sdk-core/judo-psm-generator-sdk-core-api/src/main/resources/dao/api/dto.builder.java.hbs (static from(...) builder); app: webshop-test generated Product.from (line not recorded); integration tests with two transactions reading the same version.

items.heading: ### Native SQL from a Custom Service
items.text: Generated table names use the `T_` prefix and columns the `C_` prefix (read the exact names from the generated changelog). An enumeration column holds the integer value of the enumeration literal, not its name, so compare native SQL against that integer.
items.evidence: target/judo-ng-read/wt/runtime__judo-tatami-base/judo-tatami-asm2rdbms/src/main/java/hu/blackbelt/judo/tatami/asm2rdbms/zeta/Asm2RdbmsZetaTransformation.java:125 (tablePrefix T_); runtime__judo-runtime-core/judo-runtime-core-dao-rdbms/src/main/java/hu/blackbelt/judo/runtime/core/dao/rdbms/query/mappers/VariableMapper.java:79 (enum parameter resolved via getEEnumLiteral((Integer))). Not settled: the 1-based 'ordinal+1' storage and HSQLDB avg() truncation (plain SQL semantics, not a platform fact)

items.heading: ## Rules for Custom Operations
items.text: An operation output may be an unmapped TO whose transient relation points at a mapped TO, for example a search result that holds mapped items. Fill the relation with the results of the mapped type's DAO; the response then carries `__signedIdentifier` for each mapped item.

items.heading: ## Interceptor Component Registration
items.text: An interceptor may also live in the application's `app` module when it must share a bundle with custom operations. Add `judo-runtime-core-dispatcher` as a `provided` dependency to the app `pom.xml`; the built-in interceptors stay in the generated `interceptors` module.

items.heading: ### Resolution order (`DefaultActorResolver`)
items.text: On the first request of a brand-new Keycloak user the principal can fail with `AUTHENTICATED_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` even when the `#_principal` interceptor inserts the actor row; the second request succeeds. An API client must repeat the first call once.
items.evidence: catalog/agent-docs/backend/authentication-guide.md:236 (actor row read on every request with a principal; authenticateByPrincipal runs only when no actor exists yet). Observed in the compose stack (WR19-8, app: ~/Projects/webshop-test deploy stack). Exact resolution order in DefaultActorResolver not yet read in judo-ng
